title: Python, pip and uv
description: Run Python, make virtual environments and install packages with pip or uv.
notes: Covers the Python of the python.org installer, the one that comes with Xcode or the Command Line Tools (/usr/bin/python3, with the Make pack), one installed with Homebrew (with the Homebrew pack), the Pythons that uv manages, and pyenv. Both packs come with this one.

Packages go into a virtual environment in the project (python3 -m venv, uv venv). The packages installed for your user (pip install --user) can be read, not changed, and uv cannot download a new Python: do both outside a session.
The one file outside these, /etc/apache2/mime.types, is there because pip stops when it is refused it: Python's table of file types reads it when it exists.
Not covered: conda, and a folder outside the project that your Python is set to look in (PYTHONPATH, a .pth file). Add such a folder by hand, or record a pack on top of this one.

recorded.by: sandbox-discover, with Python 3.14 from python.org, Python 3.9 of Xcode 27 and uv, then the same under the pack's folders alone; pyenv and a Homebrew Python were not tried
recorded.command: python3 main.py; python3 -m venv .venv && .venv/bin/pip install six; uv venv && uv pip install six && uv run python
